title: Raga Bairari
hookLine: a short raga whose first hymn tells the mind to listen to a story that can't be told

cards: Small things can shine brightest in a room. A candle flame hides under a cupped hand, yet in the dark, eyes go straight to it. Some sections of the Guru Granth Sahib run on page after page.
Today's isn't one of them. Raga Bairari is short enough to read in one sitting, and it comes right after Todi. But small doesn't mean dim.
Its first hymn opens with a command to the mind and a subject bigger than any book. Today: Raga Bairari.

teach.b: Bairari's hymns come from Guru Ram Das, mahala four, with Guru Arjan's voice there too. The first one opens: sun man, akath katha har naam. Sun: listen.
Man: mind, the restless inner voice the Gurus speak to again and again. Akath: what can't be spoken. Katha: a story, a telling.
Har naam: the Lord's Name. In paraphrase: listen, mind, to the untellable story of the Lord's Name. Stop on that phrase.

Akath katha, an untellable telling: a story no one can finish saying, and yet the hymn asks you to listen to it. That's the brightness inside a small raga. The section is short, but what it points to has no edge.
The hymn goes on, in paraphrase: through the Guru's teaching, meditate on the Lord, and peace and every kind of good will come.
Notice that the first word isn't sing, or bow, or give. It's listen. The mind is told to stop talking and take something in.
A short section is easy to hear whole, start to finish, and tomorrow that's exactly the plan.
Small, because the pages are few.
Bright, because of what they hold.

how: Shabads from the short Bairari section of the Guru Granth Sahib are sung in Raga Bairari in kirtan, and because the section is brief, a reader can go through all of it in one sitting.

o: a morning raga sung only at weddings and births

games.q: word by word — tap the pairs.

s: Bairari runs on for page after page
it's a short section, short enough to read in one sitting.
Bairari's first hymn opens with the word listen
sun man: listen, mind, to the untellable story of the Lord's Name.
akath katha means a story everyone already knows
akath is what can't be spoken: an untellable story the mind is still asked to hear.

games.q: you're opening a short raga with one command to the mind. which word does the hymn choose?
games.why: sun man: listen, mind. the first move in Bairari is to stop talking and take something in.

practice: Say the hymn's first two words to yourself, sun man, listen, mind, and then do it: stop rehearsing and planning, and take in the sounds, the breath and the stillness under them.
When the inner voice starts talking again, say sun man once more, gently, and go back to listening, with Waheguru as the one word you listen for, if you pray.

wordCard.voice: Raga Bairari. The short section after Todi, whose first hymn says sun man, listen, mind, to the untellable story of the Lord's Name. Today's word.
